narrative.overview: Frontier is drawn as a reviewer's desk: work is staged, labelled, and held for approval before anything runs. The page reads like a precise editorial surface — a centred sheet bounded by visible hairline rules, sections ruled off from one another, and every command and status set in monospace so it reads as a record, not decoration. The whole system exists to make one promise legible: nothing changes your files until you say go. The mood is calm, confident, and editorial, closer to a well-set documentation site or a financial ledger than a typical dev-tool landing page. Colour is rationed hard — crimson is the one saturated voice and it is spent on the single most important action in view. This world rejects the AI-SaaS defaults: no purple-to-blue gradients, no glows, no floating drop-shadowed cards, no three-up card rows. Depth comes from hairlines and tonal surfaces, not elevation.
keyCharacteristics: A centred 1280px shell with visible left/right rules; sections divided by top hairlines.
Crimson (#AF144B) as the only saturated hue, used sparingly.
Inter for everything readable; Fira Code for every label, command, tag, and number.
Flat by doctrine — hairlines and off-white surfaces instead of shadows.
Exactly one bold element per view (the hero headline).

rules.name: The One Red Column Rule
rules.body: Crimson is the single saturated hue, and at most one fully-saturated crimson mark appears per view. Tints and the channel dots are muted on purpose so the one red mark keeps its weight.

rules.name: The Mono Label Rule
rules.body: If it is a command, a status, a number, a step index, or a category, it is set in Fira Code. If it is a sentence, it is set in Inter. Nothing in between.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no glow, no gradient — ever. A surface that needs to stand out gets a hairline or a tonal fill, not elevation.

dos: Do keep crimson rare — one saturated crimson mark per view, on the single most important action.
Do set every command, status, number, and category in Fira Code; everything readable in Inter.
Do build structure from 1px hairlines and off-white surfaces, and keep the shell's side-rules visible.
Do put every padding, margin, gap and size on the 4px grid.
Do pair any channel colour with a text label; the dot alone never carries meaning.
Do keep exactly one bold element per view (the hero headline on the landing page).
donts: Don't use shadows, glows, or gradients of any kind.
Don't place three equal cards in a row; vary spans or use a dense ruled table.
Don't reach for a purple-to-blue AI palette; the channel purple is a muted outline swatch, not a decorative gradient.
Don't add a second saturated element that competes with the hero headline or the one crimson action.
Don't use arbitrary off-grid values (13px, p-[7px]).
